sectors.note:
**TL;DR:** Financials emerge as the sole sector with perfect multi-timeframe breadth, while defensive sectors like Consumer Defensive and Utilities suffer the sharpest weekly declines.

The market shows clear bifurcation as defensive sectors fade and cyclicals show selective rotation. Energy (momentum 0.817) and Technology (momentum 0.800) maintain their absolute dominance at the top of the YTD rankings. However, the Financial sector (momentum 0.70) is demonstrating the highest-quality breadth, standing as the only group out of 11 to register positive performance across all timeframes (week, month, quarter, half, and YTD).

Meanwhile, defensive groups are under pressure. Consumer Defensive fell 2 spots to rank 7 with a weak 0.33 momentum score, and Utilities slipped 1 spot to rank 9 with a market-low momentum of 0.13. On the positive side, Basic Materials (+1 spot to rank 5) and Healthcare (+1 spot to rank 8) joined Financials in making minor upward rank adjustments over the last five sessions.

## Strength
* **Broad-Based Financial Strength:** Financials (momentum 0.70) is the only sector out of 11 to achieve "all-green" status, showing positive performance across the week, month, quarter, half, and YTD.
* **Energy Dominance:** Energy remains the top-ranked sector (rank 1 YTD) with a leading momentum score of 0.817.
* **Tech Holding Strong:** Technology retains its high-momentum status at 0.800, securing the rank 2 YTD spot.

## Movers & Momentum
* **Defensive Retreat:** Consumer Defensive experienced the sharpest weekly decline, dropping 2 spots to rank 7 with a momentum score of 0.33. Utilities also fell 1 spot to rank 9 (momentum 0.13).
* **Incremental Gainers:** Basic Materials (rank 5, momentum 0.40), Financials (rank 6, momentum 0.70), and Healthcare (rank 8, momentum 0.47) each improved their ranking by +1 spot over the last 5 sessions.
* **Lagging Sectors:** Utilities (0.13) and Consumer Defensive (0.33) anchor the bottom of the momentum rankings, followed by Consumer Cyclical (rank 11, momentum 0.43).

## Divergences
* **Rank vs. Momentum Mismatch:** Financials hold "all-green" breadth status despite being ranked 6th YTD (momentum 0.70), showing stronger short-to-medium term setup than higher-ranked Real Estate (rank 4, momentum 0.53).
* **No Fragile All-Green Signals:** There are currently no sectors flagged with fragile all-green status or early-warning divergences in the data.

industries.note:
**TL;DR:** Cyclical leaders like Electronics & Computer Distribution and Steel anchor a solid market breadth of 28 all-green groups, even as aggressive rotations fuel massive gains in Internet Retail and sharp declines in Consumer Electronics.

US industry groups are exhibiting a clear division between established cyclical strength and rapid tactical rotations. Traditional leaders continue to hold the line, with Electronics & Computer Distribution (momentum 0.93) and Steel (momentum 0.91) maintaining their all-green status and dominating multi-month rankings. They are supported by robust momentum in Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing (0.888) and Computer Hardware (0.858), signaling sustained appetite for core industrial and technology infrastructure.

Beneath this steady surface, capital is rotating aggressively. Internet Retail has staged a massive near-term turnaround, leaping 55 spots in rank, while Software - Infrastructure and Internet Content & Information also booked significant rank improvements. Conversely, former favorites are feeling the chill: Consumer Electronics dropped 29 spots and Lodging shed 21 spots, while high-momentum segments like Healthcare Plans and Railroads are showing early signs of fatigue.

## Strength
* **Healthy Breadth:** 28 of 144 industry groups maintain all-green status, showing positive performance across weekly, monthly, quarterly, half-year, and YTD horizons.
* **Sustained Leadership:** Electronics & Computer Distribution (momentum 0.93) and Steel (momentum 0.91) lead the all-green cohort, showing persistent top-36 rankings across 1-, 3-, and 6-month periods.
* **Broad-Based Support:** Other highly resilient all-green industries include Department Stores (momentum 0.84), Staffing & Employment Services (momentum 0.83), and Scientific & Technical Instruments (momentum 0.79).

## Movers & Momentum
* **Top Gainers:** Internet Retail surged +55 spots to rank 53 (momentum 0.74), while Shell Companies (+44 spots, rank 35, momentum 0.62) and Software - Infrastructure (+34 spots, rank 90, momentum 0.70) also posted major weekly improvements.
* **Top Losers:** Consumer Electronics fell -29 spots to rank 61 (momentum 0.56), followed by steep declines in Lodging (-21 spots, rank 69, momentum 0.37) and Agricultural Inputs (-18 spots, rank 56, momentum 0.30).
* **Momentum Extremes:** Electronics & Computer Distribution (0.928) and Steel (0.914) remain the strongest momentum leaders, whereas Gambling (0.105) and Advertising Agencies (0.114) continue to anchor the bottom as the market's deepest laggards.

## Divergences
* **Fading Leaders:** High-momentum groups showing early signs of distribution include Healthcare Plans (momentum 0.67, rank -4), Railroads (momentum 0.69, rank -4), and Financial Conglomerates (momentum 0.75, rank -3).
* **Emerging Turnarounds:** Several low-momentum groups are quietly climbing in rank, led by Education & Training Services (+8 spots, momentum 0.49), Lumber & Wood Production (+6 spots, momentum 0.49), and Grocery Stores (+5 spots, momentum 0.28).
